cases.customer_question: How can a qualification update proceed when consistency-check errors appear after combining a new Host/Profile qualification with an existing Controller qualification?
question_variants: Why does the consistency check fail after updating Host and Profile layers?
Can RF/RF PHY layer selection avoid consistency-check errors?
How do I resolve Host/Profile and Controller layer mismatches?
What should be removed when LE Audio related consistency errors appear?
How can TCWs be used during qualification consistency resolution?
cases.actual_issue: Combining a newly qualified Host/Profile design with an existing Controller design produced consistency-check errors related to layer and feature dependencies. The qualification needed to be restructured to remove unsupported functionality and satisfy the Bluetooth SIG validation process.
cases.plain_english_explanation: When Bluetooth layers from different qualifications are combined, the Bluetooth SIG tools verify that the declared features match each other. New Host/Profile functionality can expose requirements that the existing Controller path does not satisfy. The solution is to create a compatible subset design and remove unsupported layers or features rather than forcing incompatible combinations.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant provided a procedure that removes specific layers and feature selections, including LE Audio related protocol/profile selections, performs a new consistency check, and then proceeds using the applicable waiver process for the remaining expected findings. The approach relies on creating a compatible subset of the included designs instead of modifying the unchanged Controller qualification. This avoids unnecessary exposure to additional qualification conflicts while allowing the update registration to proceed.
cases.decision_logic: Consistency validation is driven by the declared ICS capabilities and layer relationships. Removing unsupported layers and features creates a design that accurately reflects the implemented functionality and satisfies consistency requirements more safely than forcing incompatible feature combinations.
cases.final_recommendation: Create a subset design that excludes unsupported layers and feature selections, rerun the consistency check, and use the approved waiver process only for the remaining expected findings identified during review.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: The qualification may fail consistency validation, additional testing requirements may be generated, or incompatible feature declarations may remain in the design hierarchy, resulting in qualification delays and rework.
